title: Person settings
description: The person file (design part 13.4): a person's plans, limits and appetite, kept outside every repository at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/human-in-the-lead/person.json (~/.config/human-in-the-lead/person.json when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset). Data only: unknown and code-running keys are refused. A key left out is not set at this layer, so the next layer or the default applies. Caps, reserves and thresholds take the strictest layer; a project may be stricter, never looser. Version 2 adds attention, version 3 adds projects.<id>.store_remote; a file is written with the lowest version that expresses it, so one that sets neither is version 1 (design part 16.5). Internal: the file itself is never committed. Its max_executors, quota and attention also travel, as settings/person.json in each project's own private store, written by hitld config write and carried by hitld store push (HITLD-148); its projects keys never leave this file.

max_executors.description: The most executors at once across all of this person's projects: their appetite for parallel agents. The effective cap is the smallest of this, the machine's max_executors, the project's execution.max_executors and the run's cap.

quota.description: Account limits, the reserve and the thresholds (design part 12.5). These were policy.json's quota keys; a project may still set a larger reserve, earlier thresholds, and run budgets (window: run).

reserve.description: The share of each limit kept for the person's own interactive use, unless a limit sets its own reserve. The largest across the layers applies.

economize_below.description: Below this headroom, prefer cheaper models and lower concurrency. The largest across the layers applies.

critical_below.description: Below this headroom, dispatch only critical-path items. The largest across the layers applies.

notify_used.description: Shares of a limit used at which a line goes into the digest. Every layer's shares apply.

forecast_hours.description: How many recent hours the burn rate is smoothed over.

limits.description: The person's declared account limits. This list replaces the default list. A project limit with the same id can only tighten one (a lower limit, hard, a larger reserve).

attention.description: The person's attention budget (design part 2, the owner's attention as a budget; part 23.5). How many decisions the system may put in front of them, how often it may interrupt, and when it may not. The system decides whether each open question goes now, in the next digest, waits, or takes its default from these (hitld rights pending). Only a sev-1 breaks quiet hours. A project may set lower ceilings in policy.json (attention.*_max); the lower value wins. Added in schema version 2.

decisions_per_digest.description: The most decisions in front of the person at once through digests: questions shown to them and not yet answered. When that many are waiting, the next questions are held, and an easy-to-undo one takes its default.

interrupts_per_day.description: The most questions sent at once, outside a digest, in any 24 hours. A question that blocks the critical path or leaves executor slots idle uses one. 0 sends none: everything waits for a digest.

quiet_hours.description: Windows in which nothing is sent at once. Each runs from `from` to `to` in the timezone below, and may cross midnight. An empty list means no quiet hours. Only a sev-1 breaks them.

from.description: The start, as HH:MM on a 24-hour clock.

to.description: The end, as HH:MM. Earlier than `from` means the window runs past midnight.

timezone.description: The IANA time zone the quiet hours are read in, such as Europe/Paris. Default: this machine's own time zone.

non_urgent_at_once.description: How many questions that are not urgent may be in front of the person at once, sent outside a digest, while they are answering quickly. Each uses an interrupt, and quiet hours hold them. 0 sends every non-urgent question in a digest.

answering_window_minutes.description: The person counts as answering quickly when they answered a question within this many minutes.

projects.description: Per project, keyed by policy.json project.id: the project's share of headroom near the reserve when several projects compete for it (design part 13.4, across projects), equal by default; and the address of its private store's remote.

share.description: A relative weight; shares are compared with each other, not with 1.

store_remote.description: The store repository this project's private store moves through (design 0003, section 8): https://host/owner/repo.git, ssh://git@host/owner/repo.git, user@host:path or an absolute path, with no password. Written by hitld store remote set. It lives here, outside every repository, because policy.json may be public; HITLD_STORE_REMOTE, when set, is used before it. Added in schema version 3.
